SMTO-EXE-0045 — An earlier job may still be using what this task needs

GUID: 0ce23bf2-e3d9-4b0c-8236-1cb6b4739c1e
Slug: resource-liveness-unobservable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO paused this task because an earlier job may still be working on the same thing, and SMTO can't tell whether it has stopped. Your new command did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this task, find the recovery card and select Wait until the job state changes. SMTO will continue on its own once the earlier job lets go. Your command has not started yet, so waiting lets it run safely once nothing else is using the same files or service.
  2. Before asking SMTO to repeat any change, look at the file, service or machine the earlier job was working on to see whether that change already happened. SMTO can't confirm what the earlier job did, so repeating it blindly could apply the same change twice.
  3. If you know the earlier job is stuck and Resolve forcefully by terminating job is available on the card, select it. Changes it already made are kept. This stops only the recorded earlier job and frees the resource so your task can go ahead.
  4. If you no longer need this task, select Stop instead. Stopping ends this task without running the waiting command.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card disappears and the task continues, or the card shows that the earlier job has ended.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and the computer running the Gateway. Don't end programs on that computer yourself and don't ask SMTO to redo the earlier change until someone confirms what it already did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway admission refused the new command because a conflicting earlier job still holds the resource and the Gateway cannot determine whether that job's process is alive (liveness_state=unknown); the new command did not run.

What this means

  • Admission found at least one conflicting resource owner with unknown liveness and refused to start the newly requested command. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Admission found at least one conflicting resource owner with unknown liveness and refused to start the newly requested command.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original blocker identity, current liveness evidence and offered recovery actions; distinguish observation failure from actual termination.

How to fix it

  • The new job was recorded as not admitted with error_kind=resource_reconciliation_required and resource_intervention_kind=liveness_unobservable; blocking_job_ids lists the conflicting jobs. Inspect those jobs on the Gateway (status or inspect), then use the run's resource-reconciliation control (wait, or reset only when the blocker is reset-eligible) instead of resubmitting; never resubmit the mutation while the blocker's outcome is unresolved.
  • Refresh the existing operation status or cancel this task. Use the advanced recovery flow only after reviewing its explicit risk confirmation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile the blocker before requesting another mutation. An unobservable process or uncertain effect is not proof that the earlier operation did nothing.

How to verify the fix

  • The original owner is reconciled, or an explicitly authorized supported recovery decision handles the recorded risk before new admission.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
